title: Lead Clinical Midwife Coordinator
summary: Oversee community mobile clinical teams, supervise rural antenatal screenings, and train frontline midwives in emergency obstetric care protocols.
aboutRole: The Lead Clinical Midwife Coordinator will direct on-the-ground mobile outreach missions in underserved communities, ensuring adherence to clinical safety standards and mentoring rural clinic midwives.
responsibilities: Lead multidisciplinary field teams during mobile clinic outreaches in remote settlements.
Conduct antenatal clinical triage and manage complex obstetric screening escalations.
Facilitate hands-on training sessions in clean delivery, hemorrhage management, and neonatal resuscitation.
Coordinate with district health authorities and referral hospital emergency wards.
Prepare monthly clinical performance reports and maternal health indicator data.
requirements: Registered Midwife (RM) with valid clinical practicing license in an African country.
Minimum 5 years of active clinical experience in primary or tertiary obstetric care.
Demonstrated experience in rural healthcare delivery and community engagement.
Strong leadership, cross-cultural communication, and team mentorship skills.
Fluency in English; knowledge of regional languages is an added advantage.

title: Telehealth Clinical Nurse Specialist
summary: Deliver real-time remote clinical consultations, triage emergency calls from rural health posts, and support digital obstetric decision-making.
aboutRole: As part of MIA's digital health team, you will be the clinical voice on our telehealth platform, providing guidance to rural midwives managing complicated labors and answering mother inquiries.
responsibilities: Provide real-time telehealth triage and second-opinion consultations for rural clinic nurses.
Review electronic patient logs and monitor post-consultation maternal outcomes.
Deliver remote case-debriefing sessions for midwives following emergency deliveries.
Collaborate with software engineers to refine clinical workflows on the MIA mobile application.
Ensure patient records adhere strictly to clinical data privacy protocols.
requirements: Registered Nurse (RN) with advanced training or diploma in midwifery or maternal health.
At least 3 years of clinical labor ward or community maternal triage experience.
Comfortable operating digital consultation software and electronic medical records.
Calm under pressure with excellent telephone and telemedicine diagnostic skills.

title: Community Maternal Health Educator
summary: Lead participatory village health literacy sessions, teach pregnancy danger signs, and guide mothers on birth preparedness.
aboutRole: Community educators are the trusted bridge between rural families and formal healthcare. You will organize maternal health circles, nutrition demonstrations, and hygiene workshops under local community trees and centers.
responsibilities: Facilitate interactive workshops on nutrition, danger signs, and antenatal care schedules.
Distribute clean delivery kits and demonstrate proper hygienic usage to families.
Support mobile clinic registration and assist elderly or illiterate mothers.
Gather community feedback to help MIA improve outreach schedules and services.
requirements: Passionate advocate for maternal and child health in underserved communities.
Background in community health, nursing, social work, or public health education.
Fluency in the local community language is essential.
Strong interpersonal skills and empathy for vulnerable families.

title: Maternal Health Epidemiology Fellow
summary: Analyze frontline maternal indicator data, evaluate field intervention outcomes, and co-author institutional research reports.
aboutRole: This fellowship offers early-career researchers and public health graduates hands-on experience analyzing large-scale grassroots maternal health datasets to inform continental policy.
responsibilities: Clean, aggregate, and analyze maternal health records collected from mobile clinics.
Prepare statistical dashboards tracking antenatal attendance and maternal complication rates.
Contribute to quarterly grant progress reports and institutional research publications.
Support data collection training for community health workers in the field.
requirements: Master's degree (MPH, MSc) in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or Global Health.
Proficiency in statistical software (R, Python, Stata, or SPSS).
Demonstrated interest in maternal and newborn health systems in Africa.
Strong academic writing and data visualization abilities.

title: Mobile Clinic Volunteer Staff Nurse
summary: Join MIA weekend mobile health teams to deliver prenatal screenings, administer vitamin supplements, and provide bedside clinical support.
aboutRole: Give your weekends and leave days to save mothers in rural settlements. Join an energetic, multidisciplinary team of clinicians delivering direct primary care.
responsibilities: Perform antenatal checkups: blood pressure, fundal height, fetal heart rate monitoring.
Administer tetanus toxoid vaccinations and dispense prenatal vitamins.
Identify high-risk pregnancies and arrange direct referral pathways.
Educate young and first-time mothers on newborn care and exclusive breastfeeding.
requirements: Qualified Nurse or Midwife with current registration in home country.
Willingness to travel to rural communities on scheduled outreach days.
Commitment to respectful, compassionate maternal care principles.

title: Grant Writing & Partnerships Officer
summary: Develop institutional grant proposals, maintain funder relationships, and prepare donor accountability dossiers.
aboutRole: Help MIA secure the institutional resources needed to scale. You will work closely with the Executive Director and Clinical Leadership to translate field impact into competitive grant proposals.
responsibilities: Identify and track funding opportunities from bilateral agencies, foundations, and trusts.
Draft comprehensive, evidence-driven grant applications and concept notes.
Coordinate with program and finance teams to prepare detailed project budgets.
Manage reporting schedules and compile milestone reports for existing grant makers.
requirements: Bachelor's or Master's degree in International Development, Public Health, or related field.
Minimum 4 years of proven grant-writing success with global health or humanitarian NGOs.
Exceptional English writing, narrative framing, and proposal packaging skills.
Familiarity with multilateral grant compliance and logical framework approaches.
